Package index

ARD spec and ARD code

The analyses of a study as a workbook – its datasets, analysis sets, analysis data and one cards / cardx call per analyses row – and the short R program it stands for (tfl_ard_code()), or that program run (tfl_build_ard()): one study ARD.

tfl_read_ard_spec() tfl_ard_spec()
Read and check an ARD definition workbook
tfl_ard_spec_template()
An empty ARD spec
tfl_ard_code()
The R code that makes the study's ARD
tfl_ard_data_names()
The data each analysis reads, by its name in the ARD program
tfl_build_ard()
Make the study's ARD from its definition
tfl_ard_for()
One output's part of the study ARD
tfl_ard_spec_hash()
A fingerprint of one output's ARD definition

Methods, statistics and functions of one’s own

What a method may name: the keywords, any cards / cardx function and its arguments, an analysis written as R (custom), a function of the study’s own.

tfl_ard_statistics()

tfl_ard_functions()

tfl_ard_args()
The arguments of one ARD function, and how each is filled in
tfl_ard_as_custom()
An analysis as R: the code of a custom analysis
tfl_ard_function_template()
Start an ARD function of one's own from a template
tfl_ard_function_info()
What the ARD functions of one's own in some R files are

The functions the programs call

The code of the functions the generated programs call as they run (the code lists on a data, the ids in front, the formats, the study ARD), which a study keeps in a file of its own: its programs run without tflspec.

tfl_helpers_code()
The functions a study's generated programs call

Data, analysis data and populations

The datasets, populations and analysis_data sheets of the ARD spec say what is read and how the analysis data are made (see tfl_read_ard_spec()); these write the line that reads a dataset and give data to try things on.

tfl_read_adam()

tfl_example_adam()
Example ADaM-like data for trying tflspec

Simulated ADaM datasets of one oncology study, XYZ-ONC-01 (Drug X vs Control), that agree with one another; its SAP and CRF outline are in system.file("sample", "onco", package = "tflspec").

adtr

adtte

Template SPEC

A report kind from a few parameters: one definition gives the table plan (tpl_*(), the A use) and the report’s items (tfl_template_expand(), the B use). Layout templates (summary) and display templates on them (demog). A report’s YAML file may be a template SPEC, template: {name, args}: tfl_resolve_output() resolves it, its program is the template’s call, and tfl_template_to_spec() writes it out as its items.

tfl_tpl()
A table or listing template's plan: one call for every template
tfl_templates()
The templates
tfl_template_expand()
Expand a template into a report's items
tfl_template_to_spec()
A template report written out as its items

Demographics: a table plan from the template demog
tpl_summary()
Continuous variables by a column key: a table plan from the layout summary

tpl_ae_pt_freq()
Adverse events by preferred term, most frequent first: the template ae_pt_freq
tpl_ae_max_grade()
Adverse events by SOC and PT at the maximum severity or grade: the template ae_max_grade
tpl_hierarchical()
A hierarchy's counts: a table plan from the layout hierarchical
tpl_disposition()
Disposition: a table plan from the template disposition
tpl_shift() tpl_lab_shift()
Shift tables: table plans from the templates shift and lab_shift
tpl_listing()
A listing: a listing plan from the layout listing
tpl_km_table()
Kaplan-Meier estimates: a table plan from the template km_table
tpl_param_change()
Parameters' value and change: a table plan from the template param_change
tpl_lab_abnormal()
Laboratory abnormalities: a table plan from the template lab_abnormal
tpl_ae_eair()
Exposure-adjusted incidence rates by SOC and PT: the template ae_eair
tpl_ancova()
An ANCOVA of the change from baseline: a table plan from the template ancova
tpl_mean_se() tpl_mean_ci()
Mean by visit: a figure from the template mean_se or mean_ci
tpl_waterfall()
Waterfall: a figure from the template waterfall
tpl_forest_hr() tpl_forest_layout()
Hazard ratio by subgroup: a forest plot from the template forest_hr
tpl_orr()
Objective response: a table plan from the template orr
tpl_stat_block()
One record's statistics over rows and columns: a table plan from the template stat_block
tpl_ae_overview()
Overview of adverse events: a table plan from the template ae_overview

Read reports' template SPECs from a workbook
tfl_write_template_yaml()
Write a report's template SPEC as its YAML file

Template SPEC, a company’s templates

A company’s templates are an R package of its own: it registers them when it is loaded (tfl_template(), usually a tflspec template with the company’s defaults), exports the function its reports’ programs call (tfl_template_run()) and tests that no parameter is the look (tfl_test_templates()). tfl_use_company_templates() writes one to start from.

tfl_template()
Register a template
tfl_param()
A template parameter
tfl_template_params()
A template's parameters
tfl_template_variant()
A template with other defaults
tfl_template_run()
Run a template: its table plan
tfl_test_templates()
Test templates: no parameter is the look, each has its type
tfl_use_company_templates()
Write a company's template package to start from

A template’s parameters by tier (required, usual, other): the value in effect and where it is from – the study standard, a variant, the layout (tfl_tpl_args(), tfl_tpl_help()) – and each table and listing template’s page and the Kaplan-Meier report types’ (km_survival, km_cumulative), ?tfl_tpl_<name>, made from the registry.
